parsed.why: Strong statutory anti-discrimination incl. public accommodations, facilities-access law and hate-crime enforcement, but national border/custody exposure and recent ballot/funding pressure cap the score.
Low-risk tier with commission-enforced anti-discrimination and a city sanctuary, no bathroom ban; but no statutory hate-crime coverage and pending sports bills leave gaps.
State bathroom law creates universal exposure in government buildings, airports and parks, with a documented arrest; care restrictions, no anti-discrimination and a travel advisory compound risk.
No bathroom ban and hate crime covers gender identity, but care bans including custody, no anti-discrimination recourse, and a surgery-required document rule for residents.
Most-protective tier: public-accommodations anti-discrimination with enforcement, hate-crime coverage, surgery-free documents and sanctuary; national border exposure still limits safety.
